response.initial_request: The smoke alarm has come away from the ceiling and needs attention.

other_sections.Attachments: No attachments are available for this case.

events.body: Reported that the smoke alarm had come away from the ceiling and needed attention. No photographs or other attachments were supplied.
Acknowledged request NBL-016 and said the agency would check the repair arrangements with the landlord before confirming next steps.

Said an inspection had noted that the alarm had been put up recently and had come down. The agency had no record of arranging that installation. Asked whether the landlord had arranged it and whether the installer could return to secure it.
Replied briefly that they would use their own electrician to have a look. No electrician's name, work scope, or visit date was provided.
Acknowledged that the landlord would arrange the work and asked for an expected completion date and confirmation once it was finished.
Advised that the landlord intended to arrange an electrician and that visit timing should be agreed with the tenant. Asked the tenant to contact the agency if there were safety concerns.
Said the electrician would contact the tenant and complete the work by the following weekend at the latest. No contractor details or confirmed appointment were included.
Asked whether the alarm had been reattached and whether anyone had contacted the tenant. The agency still had no completion confirmation.

Tenant said the landlord had not yet fixed the alarm and that work was expected on Sunday, 31 August. The call did not establish who had confirmed that date or whether a timed appointment was arranged.

Tenant said a fitter, not the landlord, had attended, removed the bracket, and could not refit the alarm because the box had no bracket in it. The alarm remained unmounted. Tenant thought the fitter might return the following day, but no appointment was confirmed.
Tenant said they were in hospital and did not wish to speak. No maintenance details were discussed during the call.

Confirmed that the alarm work was not finished. Tenant said the fitter had been due on Sunday, but they had been admitted to hospital on Friday. They expected to arrange it when home and said they would email once it was done; for now they needed to recover.

Said the fitter had still not completed the alarm and that they had just been discharged from hospital. Tenant said they would arrange it and report when complete, and asked the agency to leave them alone for the moment because repeated calls and emails while they were ill had been upsetting.

events.to: Dorian Pike (Maintenance Operations Lead, Northbridge Lettings)
events.body: Recorded a pause in tenant contact in response to the tenant's request while they recovered. There was no evidence on file that the alarm had been mounted or tested.

Reported an unannounced person knocking at the property on Saturday morning and saying they were there to check something. Tenant did not let the person in because they could not verify who they were and thought it might be a scam. Tenant was unsure whether the visitor was connected to the alarm work.

events.to: Dorian Pike (Maintenance Operations Lead, Northbridge Lettings)
events.body: Recorded the tenant's account that they had previously raised the unexpected knock with another agency contact, who said it had been passed to a building-management contact. The visitor's identity, organization, purpose, and authority have not been verified in this case.

events.to: Dorian Pike (Maintenance Operations Lead, Northbridge Lettings)

args.subject: 26 Tallowmere Close, Fenbarrow, ZZ1 1ZZ - smoke alarm still not mounted
args.body: Dear Mr Vale, the smoke alarm at 26 Tallowmere Close, Fenbarrow, ZZ1 1ZZ is still not mounted. On 2 September the tenant said a fitter had attended, removed the bracket and could not refit the alarm. The box had no bracket in it. We have no completion confirmation. Please reply with: (1) the electrician's or fitter's name and contact details; (2) whether they sent anyone to the property around Saturday 20 September; (3) a firm date for refitting and testing the alarm. The tenant has been unwell and has asked us to limit contact, so please deal with us rather than the tenant for now. Because this is a smoke alarm, we need to hear back as soon as possible. If you would rather we arranged a contractor, please tell us.

args.reason: Safety item unresolved for about 6 weeks, landlord's contractor unidentified, an unverified visitor at the property, and the tenant is vulnerable and has asked for reduced contact.

handover_note.known: Tenant reported on 7 Aug 2025 that the smoke alarm at 26 Tallowmere Close, Fenbarrow, ZZ1 1ZZ had come down (ev 1). The agency has no record of arranging the original install (ev 3). On 7 Aug the landlord said he would use his own electrician (ev 4). On 12 Aug he said the work would be done by the following weekend (ev 7). The tenant said on 2 Sep that a fitter attended, removed the bracket and could not refit the alarm because the box had no bracket (ev 10). The alarm is still unmounted as of 11 Sep (ev 13, 14). The tenant was in hospital from about 5 Sep and was discharged by 11 Sep. They asked for no repeated contact and said they would report when done (ev 12, 13). On 20 Sep an unannounced person knocked and said they were there to check something. The tenant did not let them in (ev 15, 16).
handover_note.conflicts: On 27 Aug the tenant said the landlord had not fixed the alarm and work was expected on 31 Aug (ev 9). On 2 Sep the tenant said a fitter, not the landlord, had attended (ev 10). The landlord's electrician has never been named, so we can't tell whether the fitter, the 20 Sep visitor and the landlord's electrician are the same party. The visitor's identity and authority are unverified (ev 16). Ev 16 says the tenant raised the knock with another agency contact, who passed it to a building-management contact. There is no record of the outcome. There is no completion confirmation. The landlord has not been chased since 12 Aug.
handover_note.done: Sent the landlord a request for the electrician's identity and contact details, whether they sent anyone on about 20 Sep, and a firm refit date. I did not contact the tenant, given their request for a pause (ev 14).
handover_note.needed: Decide who owns this: chase the landlord by phone, or have the agency arrange a contractor for the smoke alarm, which is a safety item. Check the identity of the 20 Sep visitor with the building-management contact. Decide on a welfare-sensitive way to contact the tenant and confirm access. Consider advising the tenant on interim safety, such as a temporary alarm. Confirm the alarm is mounted and tested before closing.

args.summary: The smoke alarm has been unmounted for about 6 weeks and the landlord's contractor has never been identified. An unverified visitor knocked on 20 Sep, and the tenant is vulnerable and wants less contact. I asked the landlord for contractor details and a firm date, and handed the case to the property manager.
facts: Tenant reported the alarm down on 7 Aug (ev 1).
Landlord said he would use his own electrician, with no name given (ev 4, 7).
A fitter attended but could not refit the alarm because the box had no bracket (ev 10).
The alarm was still unmounted on 11 Sep (ev 13, 14).
The tenant was hospitalised and asked for reduced contact (ev 11-13).
An unverified visitor knocked on 20 Sep (ev 15, 16).
conflicts: The tenant said the landlord's work was expected on 31 Aug (ev 9), but later said a fitter, not the landlord, attended (ev 10).
The landlord's electrician, the fitter and the 20 Sep visitor cannot be matched, because no contractor was ever named.
Ev 16 says the knock was passed to a building-management contact, but the outcome is unrecorded.
missing: Confirmation that the alarm is mounted and tested.
The identity and authority of the 20 Sep visitor.
options_rejected: Wait: this is a safety item and it has already drifted for weeks.
Ask only: the safety risk, the unverified visitor and the vulnerable tenant need the property manager's decision.
Contact the tenant: they asked for a pause in contact (ev 13, 14).
Close: there is no completion evidence.
args.uncertainty: The landlord may reply and settle the contractor question, but the safety and welfare issues still need the property manager.
